search.description: This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica).* BoPep4 acts as a peptide hormone and signaling molecule to regulate plant defense mechanisms and salt tolerance. The BoPep4 coding sequence was codon-optimized for *B. subtilis*.

## **About**

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 

## Dry lab / computational analysis

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/db789e4a-bc1e-43a6-8afd-de6ca8e4cbc4/b8766a706c1563004798167ebc968c6c37fb1bdc8ab7e6f71e9a6c0a198a09bd.avif)

**Figure ST-3. BoPep4 bound to the plant receptor PEPR1.** (a) The PEPR1 ectodomain, residues 29-738 (710 modelled), shown as a grey surface, with BoPep4 — BoPep4 1-23, Gly1 to Asn23 — in orange, lying in the inner groove of the leucine-rich-repeat solenoid. This is the starting structure of every molecular dynamics run in this document, threaded onto the 5GR8 (PEPR1-AtPep1) crystal structure of PEPR1 with AtPep1. Teal patches are the eight crystallographic contact residues: Asp273, Val297, Asp348, Phe371, Asp441, Ile443, Asn465, Arg487. (b) The Asn23 clamp, the interaction the peptide works through. The free C-terminal carboxylate of Asn23 is gripped by the Arg487 guanidinium (orange dashes); Asn465 and Asp441 complete the clamp. This is the contact that the molecular dynamics tracks, and the one a C-terminal purification tag destroys. BoPep4 is a 23-amino-acid plant elicitor peptide from broccoli. Binding PEPR1 switches on the plant's own salt-tolerance response, so a small amount of secreted peptide produces a plant-side effect. The pose is a model, not an experimental structure of BoPep4 with PEPR1.

documentation.title: Application
documentation.value:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **BoPep4 2.1 (**[<u>BBa\_26LYCBW0</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26lycbw0)): In this variant, the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.
* **BoPep4 2.2 (**[<u>BBa\_26ERHWWI</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26erhwwi)): This is a second optimized variant of the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 coding sequence, designed with the same aim of improving the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.
* **SamyQ-BoPep4-Histag** ([<u>BBa\_26ILD3SO</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ild3so)): The BoPep4 protein, a C-terminally encoded plant elicitor peptide derived from broccoli, is fused to the SamyQ signal peptide at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus.
* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-BoPep4-Histag-B0015** ([<u>BBa\_26FSZTWM</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26fsztwm)): this Protectant Module constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS0, and terminator B0015.
